stories.headline: FAA halts every US departure in third-ever nationwide ground stop
stories.dek: A communications failure across air traffic control centers grounded flights for hours Friday, and the Transportation Secretary blames decades-old analog equipment.
stories.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration stopped departures from every US airport on Friday afternoon, only the third nationwide ground stop in its history. The stop began at 3:36 pm EST, and domestic flights were cleared to take off again at 8:35 pm EST, according to Ars Technica.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy first announced the stop on X, citing a "communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers." After it was lifted, he blamed aging infrastructure. "Today's nationwide ground stop happened because our air traffic control system is operating on DECADES-OLD analog equipment that simply cannot compete with the demands of the 21st century," Duffy wrote, warning there will be "more of these" without major system updates. PCMag also reports that the outage is tied to air traffic control upgrades.

Over a million travelers were affected, Ars Technica reports. Some airlines canceled flights for the rest of Friday. Air Canada canceled all flights to and from the United States for the evening. While departures were halted, controllers handled landings on what Homeland Security's Markwayne Mullin called "a case-by-case basis," with communication systems working "at certain levels" but "overwhelmed."

Mullin told reporters the event "is not a threat to the US" and described it as a telecommunications outage, according to TechRadar. Officials said there was no indication of a nefarious attack, but Mullin said they were not ruling anything out. He saw no reason to connect it to a large Microsoft Outlook outage the day before, and Microsoft said it had no indication its services were involved.

The timing raised questions about the FAA's AI-backed SMART routing system, which the agency announced it was expanding to more airports a day earlier. TechRadar notes that rollout began in September, so any link is conjecture. Pilot and YouTuber Scott Manley suggested a more ordinary cause: a failure limiting en route centers' ability to hand off flight information to each other as aircraft cross the country.

The exact technology that failed has not been publicly detailed.
key_points: FAA stopped all US departures from 3:36 pm to 8:35 pm EST Friday
Over a million travelers affected; Air Canada canceled US flights for the evening
Duffy blames decades-old analog air traffic control equipment
Officials saw no sign of an attack but did not rule one out
stories.why_it_matters: A single communications failure grounded a whole country's air traffic, a stark example of legacy infrastructure as a single point of failure. Anyone with US travel plans should expect Duffy's warned "more of these" until the system is modernized.

stories.headline: Microsoft apologizes for global outage, says AI and hackers not to blame
stories.dek: The company traces the Microsoft 365 failure to a network upgrade issue, as a former UK cyber chief calls it possibly worse than CrowdStrike.
stories.body:
Microsoft has apologized for the global outage that disrupted Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and Copilot, starting November 12. "We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners," the company said, according to PC Gamer. Microsoft says the failure was "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents," introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a recent network change.

The company says it has fixed the underlying problem and is seeing broad recovery. It extended email timeouts to 48 hours to preserve delayed mail, and promises a full post-incident report.

Ciaran Martin, former head of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre, told NBC News it looks like "one of the biggest outages of all time," possibly worse than recent AWS and CrowdStrike incidents, Ars Technica reports. Hospitals, banks, courts and Japan's government were affected.
key_points: Microsoft says the outage stemmed from a network capacity upgrade issue, not AI or malicious activity.
The company apologized, reports broad recovery and promises a full post-incident report.
Former UK NCSC head Ciaran Martin suggested the outage may be worse than the AWS and CrowdStrike incidents.

sources.title: Trezor Confirms Hidden Implants in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallets That Can Steal Recovery Phrases

stories.headline: Trezor confirms recovery-phrase implants in three Safe 5 wallets
stories.dek: Devices sold by reseller CryptoBilis hid an extra circuit board that sent seed words over cellular networks; firmware 2.13.1 now blocks it.
stories.body:
Trezor has confirmed that three Safe 5 hardware wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained malicious implants built to steal recovery phrases. The extra circuit board sits between the main board and the display, reads seed words and passphrases shown on screen, encrypts them and sends them over a mobile network to an attacker-controlled server. It leaves the wallet's firmware and Secure Element untouched.

Firmware 2.13.1, released November 11, stops the known implants from capturing anything, but cannot protect phrases already stolen. Trezor advises CryptoBilis buyers since March to move funds to a new wallet with a new phrase, and offers free replacements. No owners have reported lost funds.

The implants mirror those Ledger found in CryptoBilis-sold devices, which were linked to thefts. Trezor has cut its reseller network by about 80 percent.
key_points: Three compromised Safe 5 wallets were bought from CryptoBilis between August 20 and September 23, 2026; 48 customers have come forward for checks.
Firmware 2.13.1 blocks the current implants but cannot undo earlier phrase theft, so Trezor urges affected buyers to move funds to a new recovery phrase.
Trezor has trimmed its reseller network by about 80 percent after similar implants were found in Ledger devices from the same reseller.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE

stories.headline: PostgreSQL patches 52 flaws, including 22-year-old code execution bug
stories.dek: Updates to 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25 fix a type-confusion flaw, but C-language extensions must be rebuilt too.
stories.body:
The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has shipped updates fixing 52 security flaws, including CVE-2026-6460, a type-confusion bug that lets a database user who can create objects run code on the server. The flaw scores 8.8 on CVSS and affects all versions before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25. Full protection also requires rebuilding any C-language extensions, The Hacker News reports.

Researcher Mehmet Ince traces the bug to a 2004 change that let columns change type. He published a writeup showing a crash and memory leak on 18.6, and says he shared proofs of concept with AWS, Microsoft, Google and others in August. No attacks have been reported.

PostgreSQL 14 is now end-of-life. Admins should also update client tools such as pg_dump and pg_restore, which had their own code-execution fixes.
key_points: CVE-2026-6460 (CVSS 8.8) lets users who can create objects run code as the PostgreSQL OS user.
Fixed in 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25; C-language extensions must be rebuilt.
32 of the 52 flaws are rated 8.8; no exploitation in the wild has been reported.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Check Point Gateways to Deploy TSGA Backdoor and Wipe ESXi Files

stories.headline: Check Point patches zero-day used for root access on its gateways
stories.dek: Attackers chained PHP2Shell bugs with a Gaia OS flaw to plant the TSGA backdoor, then pivoted to VMware ESXi hosts and ran a wiper.
stories.body:
Check Point has released emergency hotfixes for CVE-2026-123039, a high-severity local privilege escalation flaw in Gaia OS that attackers have exploited since late October. The company says it saw active exploitation against "a couple of dozen customers." The bug sits in the DynamicCLI daemon, which runs as root and accepts unauthenticated commands on a world-writable local socket.

According to Check Point, attackers first broke into Mobile Access portals using the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, then used the new flaw to gain root. They deployed web shells and the TSGA backdoor, moved to VMware ESXi hosts over SSH and ran a wiper called destroy_v6. The first wave, starting October 30, hit Israeli organizations. A broader wave followed on November 2.

Check Point links TSGA to a China-nexus toolkit but says it cannot attribute the campaign with high confidence. Admins who can't patch should stop the dynamic_server process.
key_points: CVE-2026-123039 (CVSS 7.8) affects Gaia OS versions R81 through R82.20 and has been exploited against roughly two dozen customers.
Attackers chained PHP2Shell bugs with the flaw to install the TSGA backdoor and wipe files on VMware ESXi hosts.
Check Point says the evidence does not allow high-confidence attribution, citing the wiper and the campaign's focus on Israel.

sources.title: Mass smuggling of up to 1.5 million Nvidia AI GPUs could be the underlying cause of Jensen Huang's departure, analysts claim

stories.headline: Singapore charges executive over 917 Nvidia AI servers as probes widen
stories.dek: Malaysia is also investigating Megaspeed's local arm, while SemiAnalysis estimates up to 1.5 million restricted Nvidia GPUs may have reached China.
stories.body:
Singapore has brought 41 criminal charges against Shi Bingzhe, a 34-year-old Chinese citizen who was director of Superphi and chief operating officer of NJ Global Financial, The Straits Times reports. Prosecutors say the two firms bought 917 servers containing restricted Nvidia hardware from Aperia International in 41 transactions between May 2024 and February 2025. The case now involves five people and six companies.

Malaysia is examining whether Speedmatrix, the local subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed, re-exported imported AI hardware, according to Reuters. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says there is no evidence it left the country. Neither probe has found that the hardware reached China.

SemiAnalysis estimates that more than 1.5 GW of restricted Nvidia hardware, possibly up to 1.5 million GPUs, has reached China. The firm links the smuggling to Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia but offers no direct evidence.
key_points: Singapore filed 41 charges against Shi Bingzhe over 917 servers with restricted Nvidia hardware; he faces up to 10 years in prison if convicted.
Malaysia is probing whether Megaspeed subsidiary Speedmatrix re-exported AI hardware; Megaspeed has hired a U.S. law firm to audit its GPU inventory.
SemiAnalysis estimates over 1.5 GW of restricted Nvidia hardware, up to 1.5 million GPUs, reached China despite U.S. export controls.

sources.title: New Mior and Skyfall Attacks Let Rogue Cloud Hosts Steal Secrets From AMD SEV-SNP VMs

stories.headline: Mior and Skyfall attacks let rogue hosts read AMD SEV-SNP VMs
stories.dek: Researchers at ETH Zurich and Google show a malicious hypervisor can pull secrets from confidential VMs on EPYC chips; firmware fixes roll out through December.
stories.body:
Two newly disclosed attacks, Mior and Skyfall, let a malicious cloud host read data inside AMD SEV-SNP confidential VMs, which are built to keep the server operator out, The Hacker News reports. Mior, from ETH Zurich, also lets an attacker modify VM memory and fake attestation reports. It needs control of the hypervisor and BIOS plus a PCIe device, and worked in all 1,000 attempts on a Zen 5 EPYC 9135.

Skyfall, from ETH Zurich and Google, builds on AMD's Transient Scheduler Attacks and needs only a malicious hypervisor. It recovered register values and a disk-encryption key on Zen 3 and Zen 4 chips.

AMD rates Mior 5.9 and Skyfall 4.9 on CVSS 4.0. Platform firmware reaches server makers in November for Skyfall and December for Mior. Renters depend on cloud providers to install it.
key_points: Mior (CVE-2026-0462) corrupts AMD's Reverse Map Table at startup and needs hypervisor, BIOS and PCIe device control.
Skyfall (CVE-2026-40671) leaks VM register data on Zen 3 and Zen 4 EPYC chips via a malicious hypervisor alone.
AMD plans platform firmware for server makers in November (Skyfall) and December (Mior); both teams have published code.
